questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white backgrounds and black letters show road rules like speed limits. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of an accident, you should:

options.text: Try to blend into traffic and not be noticed by other drivers.
Not use turn signals unless you are traveling at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Ride closely to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, be visible to other drivers. Use your turn signals, brake lights, and proper lane position to show what you plan to do. Keep enough space between you and other vehicles. Look ahead 12 seconds and be ready for hazards.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than riding during the day because you can more easily see the lights of other vehicles.
More difficult than riding during the day because it is harder to see.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than riding during the day because it is harder to see.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because you cannot see as well and others cannot see you as well. It is also harder to judge distances at night.

questions.question: Which color is best to wear to be seen?
questions.correctAnswerText: Orange
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green. These colors make you easier to see while riding at any time of day.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume the passenger has traveled by motorcycle before.
Not assume the passenger has traveled by motorcycle before and explain the process.
Not bother with explaining anything since they are only a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the passenger has traveled by motorcycle before and explain the process.
questions.explanation: Your passenger needs to know how to stay safe. Do not assume they have ridden a motorcycle before. Give full instructions before every ride.

questions.question: The most important thing you can do to survive a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is fastened properly is the best way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: It is best to not ride directly alongside another vehicle because:

options.text: You may be riding in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be difficult to see what is happening behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be riding in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside a vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape path if danger appears.

questions.question: To get the best protection, be sure your helmet:
questions.correctAnswerText: Meets Department of Transportation guidelines.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all around and have no obvious damage.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Try to squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. Your motorcycle will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more space to stop. Ride more slowly, start braking sooner, leave more space between vehicles, and wait for bigger gaps when turning or merging.

questions.question: Most motorcycles:

options.text: Have brakes in both the front and rear.
Have three brakes: one in the front, one in the rear, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have brakes in both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Set up and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
Ride the same way you would alone.
Make sure footrests are only for you, the driver.
Tell the passenger what to do after you start riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set up and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Only carry a passenger if your motorcycle is set up for it. Your motorcycle needs a separate seat for two people, footrests for the passenger, and you may need to adjust the headlight, tire pressure, and suspension for the extra weight.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your blood alcohol level or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not change how much alcohol is in your system.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast:

options.text: Is okay if you stay under the speed limit.
Is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
Is okay if no other vehicles are nearby.
Can cause you to drift into another lane or off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to drift into another lane or off the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. If you go too fast, you may slide into another lane or off the road. Always slow down for turns.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Front and rear
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel: a front brake and a rear brake. The front brake provides more stopping power than the rear brake.

questions.question: Which of the following does not need to be checked regularly?
questions.correctAnswerText: The paint
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Small problems on a motorcycle can be very dangerous when riding.

questions.question: If you drink only one alcoholic drink:

options.text: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
Your body is usually not affected.
Your body is affected, but only for a short time.
Your body is affected, but coffee can fix it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can hurt your ability to ride safely. Your body can only get rid of alcohol with time. Nothing else can speed up this process.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Be worn only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn day and night.
questions.explanation: Wear bright and reflective clothing at all times to help other drivers see you. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so bright clothing is important then too.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Not be worn during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn at night.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials to be more visible, especially at night. Bright clothing with reflective materials helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: What is the main active ingredient in marijuana?
questions.correctAnswerText: THC
questions.explanation: The main active ingredient in marijuana is THC (tetrahydrocannabinol).

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause hearing loss.
questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise while riding can damage your hearing. Wear proper hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is made safer by wearing reflective clothing.
Is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only be done in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is made safer by wearing reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing when riding at night. This makes other drivers see you better.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the impact. This keeps you from being thrown off the motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Always scan the road ahead and expect potential risks.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because they are rare on the road.
Look ahead but try not to look for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always scan the road ahead and expect potential risks.
questions.explanation: Look well ahead while riding to see potential hazards early. This helps you react before you reach them.

questions.question: If possible, do not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: Another driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle may block your way to escape if hazards appear.
